description: crate-jmap-mail-server/tests/common/mod.rs:2361: the string 'rfc822; test@example.com' is hardcoded as the final_recipient test value. The 'rfc822' prefix is an RFC 2298 / RFC 8098 address-type token, but this is not explained anywhere near the constant. A maintainer unfamiliar with RFC 8098 §3.2 would not know whether 'rfc822;' is a magic string, a placeholder, or a normative requirement. Fix: add a comment citing RFC 8098 §3.2 (Original-Recipient and Final-Recipient address-type syntax).
title: Document rfc822 address-type prefix in MemoryBackend send_mdns
